name: str_detect
title: Detect the presence or absence of a match

origin.description: Return TRUE for each element of string that matches pattern, and FALSE otherwise. This is the same test as grepl.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares bytes, and coll uses the locale's collation rules. The empty string and boundary patterns are not allowed.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, invert the logical result. Must be a single TRUE or FALSE.

origin.details: The inputs follow vctrs recycling: a length-1 vector is repeated, including down to length 0, and any other disagreeing lengths are an error. A missing string stays missing. Names on string are copied when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string. A missing pattern is an error. negate does not turn a missing result into a match.
origin.value: A logical vector the same length as the common size of string and pattern.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_detect(fruit, "a")
writeLines(paste0('str_detect(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "a") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Return true for each element of string that matches pattern, and false otherwise.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, and regex return Pattern objects and select that engine. The empty string and boundary are errors.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, invert each real match. Must be True or False.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. Length 1 is recycled, including down to 0. pattern_type chooses the engine and pattern_opts supplies opts_regex, opts_fixed, or opts_collator. Empty calls no_empty and bound calls no_boundary. A missing string is NA. Names on string are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA. JSON null is that missing value.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_detect
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_detect(fruit, "a")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('str_detect(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "a") returns ' + words + '.')
